title: Aggregates, repositories and events
idea: An aggregate is a cluster of domain objects changed as one unit through a single root, which guards the rules that must always hold.
points: Outside code holds references only to the root, never to inner objects.
A repository stores and finds whole aggregates by the root's id.
Domain events record facts, like `OrderPlaced`, for other parts to react to.
A domain service holds logic that belongs to no single aggregate.

messages.label: find(O-1)
messages.note: The service loads order O-1 by its root id. It already holds 2 pens; the limit is 3.

messages.label: Order
messages.note: It gets the root back. Inner lines come with it, never on their own.

messages.label: addLine(pad, 1)
messages.note: Every change goes through the root, which checks the rules first.

messages.label: new Line
messages.note: Only the root creates and holds its lines.

messages.label: addLine(ink, 1)
messages.note: Pens plus pad make 3 units. One more ink would make 4, so the root refuses it.

messages.label: place()
messages.note: Placing records an `OrderPlaced` domain event inside the aggregate.

messages.label: save(order)
messages.note: The service saves the whole aggregate in one step.

messages.label: OrderPlaced
messages.note: After saving, the event goes to listeners such as billing, outside the aggregate.

code.title: An Order aggregate
code.caption: `Order` is the root. Its unit limit holds no matter who calls, because every change passes through it.

walk.text: Fields are private; no getter exposes the live list of lines.
`addLine` is the only way in. It checks state and the unit limit first.
Placing records a domain event instead of calling other code directly.
The repository saves and finds whole orders by id, never single lines.
The loaded root accepts the pad but refuses the ink: three units is the limit.
Events are handed out as a copy, ready for the caller to publish.

pitfalls: Do not return the live inner list; callers could bypass the root's checks.
Keep aggregates small; refer to other aggregates by id, not by object.
Change one aggregate per transaction; let a domain event update the others.

quiz.q: Using `Order` above, what does this print?
quiz.why: `place` set the order to placed, so `addLine` throws `placed` before checking units.

takeaway: Change an aggregate only through its root; load and save it whole.

starters: How do I decide where an aggregate boundary goes?
When should I use a domain service instead of a method on an entity?
How are domain events published after saving?
